Subject: Translation partner contract extension — scope & pricing

Hi Ana,

Hope you're well — our current SOW with TranslateCo runs out at the end of July. We'd like to discuss a 12-month extension that covers both product UI strings and docs localization (API docs, self-serve guides). Usage has shifted toward more docs-heavy localization over the past year, so we'd like the next contract to reflect:

- Clear per-word and per-string pricing tiers (UI short strings vs technical docs)
- Turnaround times (TAT) for urgent UI pushes (2 business-hours SLA for critical strings)
- Monthly word cap with burst/billable overage terms
- Support for pseudo-localization and context screenshots for engineers
- A single SOW and an easier signature flow (DocuSign preferred)

Could you send a revised SOW and indicative pricing? Attach any typical SLA language and where possible include credits for quality regressions (we've had a couple of issues in es-ES last quarter).

Cc'ing Marissa (engineering localization partner) and Laura (procurement) so we can route details. If TranslateCo can provide a version of the SOW plus a quick pricing summary by next Friday (June 18), we can kick off legal review the same day.

Thanks —
Marcus
VP, Developer Platforms
Redwood Inference

Hi Marcus — thanks for the note and for outlining the priorities. We can absolutely support a consolidated 12-month SOW that covers both UI strings and documentation. I've attached a draft SOW (TranslateCo_SOW_v3.pdf) and a one-page pricing summary. High-level:

- UI strings (short-form): $0.04/string for volumes up to 50k strings/mo; urgent SLA (2 business hours) available as an add-on at $500/mo.
- Technical docs (per-word): $0.06/word with tiered discounts after 200k words/mo.
- Monthly blended cap option: $75k/mo (covers a mixed workload; overage billed at 1.2x standard rates).
- Quality credits: we offer a two-tier remediation credit for verified errors (5% credit on the invoice for repeat language issues).

We included a clause for pseudo-localization and a checkbox for attaching context screenshots. The attached SOW includes standard delivery SLAs; the legal team can reduce the TAT language for urgent UI items into a separate appendix if Redwood prefers.

I'll highlight areas we think will need redlines from your side: billing cadence, definition of "urgent string", and data handling for screenshots.

If this looks reasonable, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet and can arrange a short call next week to walk through redlines.

Best,
Ana Costa
Head of Strategic Accounts
TranslateCo

Marcus / Laura — quick internal notes after a first pass on Ana's SOW:

- Good: consolidated SOW and blended cap option; pricing in the expected range.
- Needs clarification: how they count "strings" (are concatenated UI keys considered a single string?) and whether screenshots are retained by TranslateCo or purged after translation. Our security policy requires purge within 30 days unless otherwise approved.
- TAT: the 2-hour urgent SLA as an add-on is fine, but we need an availability window (e.g., business hours PST / EST) and a max per-month cap so they don't charge the add-on for every small request.
- Quality: the 5% credit is a start but ambiguous — propose a measurable SLA: error rate threshold (e.g., <1.5% verified issues per language per month) with a clearly defined verification process.
- Ramp: we will likely increase docs volume starting Q4 (API product launches). If we take the blended cap, negotiate a 60-day commit to allow us to ramp with limited overage exposure.

Action items:
- Laura: can procurement confirm whether a 12-month term with a 60-day ramp is acceptable (and flag any payment term concerns)?
- Monica: please review the data handling clause in the SOW attachment — look for retention, encryption, subprocessor disclosures.

I can draft a redline suggestion for the TAT and quality metrics by Wednesday.

- Marissa
Senior Localization Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Ana — thanks for the SOW and pricing summary. Internal feedback below and a request for a revised SOW that incorporates our redlines (I've attached a short redline doc to Drive):

Summary of our asks (for the revised SOW):
1) Definitions: clearly separate "UI short strings" (<= 200 characters) from "Technical docs" and include counting rules for concatenated keys.
2) Data handling: purge screenshots and any customer PII within 30 days; confirm AES-256 at-rest encryption and SOC 2 evidence.
3) TAT & availability: urgent SLA (2 business hours) to apply Mon-Fri 8am-6pm PT; add monthly cap of 60 urgent requests included in the add-on.
4) Quality SLA: define verification workflow and target <=1.5% verified issues per locale/month with a 7-day remediation window; provide remediation credit schedule.
5) Pricing & ramp: accept 12-month term with a 60-day ramp where overages are charged at 0.8x the standard overage rate for the ramp period.

If TranslateCo can send a revised SOW reflecting the above and a DocuSign packet by Tuesday (June 23), Legal will prioritize review. We'll proceed with a 12-month extension at the pricing Ana proposed subject to those redlines and legal sign-off.

I've added Monica to help expedite the security checklist. Laura — please flag any procurement concerns on payment terms. Marissa — if you want me to push for additional credits for languages that hit quality regressions, say the word.

Thanks —
Marcus
VP, Developer Platforms
Redwood Inference
